core_obligations: Define the comparison maps H^p(X,F) tensor H^q(Y,G) -> H^n(X times Y, pr_1^*F tensor pr_2^*G) from functoriality of cohomology together with the cup product (proof lines 5460-5478).
Settle the affine case using the vanishing of higher cohomology of quasi-coherent modules on affines and the definitions of pullback and tensor product (proof lines 5479-5483).

Choose finite affine open coverings U of X and V of Y, form the product covering W of X times Y, and use that W refines both pr_1^{-1}U and pr_2^{-1}V to obtain maps of Cech complexes and hence of their cohomology (proof lines 5486-5496 and following).

Identify the Cech complex of W for pr_1^*F tensor pr_2^*G with the tensor product of the complexes of U and V, apply Kunneth for complexes over a field, and conclude the displayed isomorphism in the stated generality (remaining lines of the proof, up to line 5630).
proof_roadmap: Produce the comparison maps via pullback and cup product.
Handle the affine case by vanishing.
Compare Cech complexes over a product covering with the tensor product of the two Cech complexes.
Conclude with Kunneth for complexes over a field.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the Kunneth isomorphism expressing the cohomology of the external tensor product of quasi-coherent modules on a product as the direct sum of tensor products of the factors, for quasi-compact schemes with affine diagonal. The proof first settles the affine case by the vanishing of higher cohomology on affines, then chooses finite affine open coverings of both factors, notes that the product covering refines both pullbacks, and compares the Cech complexes of the three coverings to obtain the Kunneth map for the Cech cohomology of the product; the identification of the resulting complex with the tensor product of the two Cech complexes (Kunneth for complexes of modules over a field) then gives the result (proof lines 5459-5630). H3: the comparison of Cech complexes over a product covering and the reduction of the algebra to the tensor product of complexes is independent research-level work, not a citation.
